question: What is the primary purpose of inserting an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To secure and maintain a patent airway
options.B: To deliver liquid nutrition directly to the stomach
options.C: To monitor continuous central venous pressure
options.D: To remove excess fluid from the pleural space

explanation: An endotracheal tube provides a direct conduit for oxygen and air into the trachea, bypassing upper airway obstructions. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: A patient with severe facial burns is admitted to the emergency department. Why might clinicians choose early endotracheal intubation?

options.A: To decrease the systemic absorption of topical burn ointments
options.B: To facilitate easier insertion of a large-bore nasogastric tube
options.C: To prevent airway collapse from rapidly developing soft tissue edema
options.D: To prepare the patient for immediate total parenteral nutrition

explanation: Thermal burns to the head and neck cause severe, fast-moving swelling that can completely close off the upper airway within hours. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the name of the triangular opening located directly between the vocal cords?
explanation: The tip of the endotracheal tube must pass directly through the glottis to enter the trachea successfully. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: Why is the Mallampati score assessed before attempting planned endotracheal intubation?

options.A: To determine the correct size of the suction catheter to use
options.B: To calculate the precise dose of sedative medication required
options.C: To estimate the visibility of oral and pharyngeal structures for intubation difficulty
options.D: To measure the functional residual capacity of the patient's lungs

explanation: A high Mallampati score indicates that the tongue and soft palate crowd the oral cavity, predicting a harder view of the vocal cords. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of inserting a stylet inside an endotracheal tube before intubation?

options.A: To measure real-time airway pressure during mechanical ventilation
options.B: To filter incoming room air and trap airborne pathogens
options.C: To give the flexible tube rigidity and shape for easier insertion
options.D: To inflate the internal cuff once the tube reaches the trachea

explanation: A malleable stylet allows the operator to bend the tube into a curve that matches the patient's upper airway anatomy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: Which piece of equipment must always be tested immediately before starting an intubation attempt?

options.A: The central venous pressure transducer monitor
options.B: The laryngoscope light source and blade lock

explanation: A dim or failing laryngoscope light will obscure the vocal cords and lead to failed or traumatic intubation attempts. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of pre-oxygenating a patient with 100% oxygen prior to intubation?

options.A: To dry up excessive oral secretions that could block the camera
options.B: To dilate the bronchial tree and ease passage of the breathing tube
options.C: To build an oxygen reserve in the lungs and delay arterial desaturation
options.D: To lower the patient's systemic blood pressure during induction

explanation: Denitrogenating the lungs buys safe time for the practitioner to place the tube without causing dangerous drops in blood oxygen levels. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why are neuromuscular blocking agents administered during rapid sequence intubation?

options.A: To stimulate spontaneous coughing and clear lower airway mucus plugs
options.B: To keep the patient completely asleep throughout a long surgical procedure
options.C: To relax jaw muscles and paralyze vocal cords for optimal tube passage
options.D: To prevent the heart rate from dropping when the laryngoscope is inserted

explanation: Paralytics eliminate laryngeal reflexes and jaw tone, making it much easier to visualize the vocal cords and insert the tube without trauma. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which hand should the clinician use to hold and manipulate the laryngoscope during insertion?
explanation: Standard laryngoscopes are designed to be held in the left hand, allowing the right hand free movement to manage the tube and suction. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is the maximum recommended time limit for a single intubation attempt to protect the patient?
explanation: Limiting attempts to roughly 30 seconds prevents prolonged interruption of ventilation and dangerous drops in blood oxygen saturation. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is considered the gold standard clinical method for confirming correct endotracheal tube placement?

options.A: Checking for symmetrical movement of the chest wall
options.B: Observing condensation inside the plastic tube wall
options.D: Listening for equal breath sounds with a stethoscope

explanation: Capnography detects exhaled carbon dioxide, proving that the tube is sitting inside the respiratory tract rather than the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: A newly intubated patient has absent breath sounds on the left side of the chest and muffled sounds on the right. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: The tube has accidentally slipped out into the upper pharynx
options.B: The tube was advanced too far and entered the right main bronchus
options.C: The endotracheal tube cuff has ruptured and is leaking air
options.D: The patient is experiencing a sudden tension pneumothorax

explanation: Because the right mainstem bronchus is straighter and wider, tubes frequently slip too deep, ventilating only the right lung. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why is oral care with antiseptic solutions essential for an intubated patient?

options.A: To prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia by reducing bacterial colonization
options.B: To keep the lips moist and prevent the endotracheal tube from sticking
options.C: To dissolve dried blood left over from the laryngoscope insertion
options.D: To stimulate the gag reflex and help the patient clear throat secretions

explanation: Good oral hygiene reduces the oral bacteria that travel down the airway around the tube cuff into the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately after securing a newly placed endotracheal tube?

options.A: Deflate the internal cuff completely to relieve pressure on the tracheal wall
options.B: Disconnect the humidification tubing to check for adequate airflow
options.C: Record the exact centimeter depth marking of the tube at the patient's lip
options.D: Turn the patient onto their side to drain pooled oral secretions

explanation: Documenting the lip line measurement provides a baseline to detect if the tube has slipped inward or outward during nursing care. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: Which sudden complication does the letter 'P' represent in the DOPE troubleshooting mnemonic?
explanation: Pneumothorax is a life-threatening collapse of a lung that causes sudden respiratory distress and hypoxia in ventilated patients. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h8)

question: An intubated patient on mechanical ventilation suddenly becomes restless, with falling oxygen saturations and high airway pressure alarms sounding. Auscultation reveals absent breath sounds on the left. What is NOT an appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Suction the endotracheal tube to clear any potential mucous plugs
options.B: Inspect the ventilator circuit to ensure all connections are tight
options.C: Check the tube depth markings at the teeth to see if it migrated
options.D: Immediately remove the endotracheal tube and leave the airway unprotected

explanation: Pulling the tube prematurely without assessing simpler causes or attempting bag ventilation can lead to complete airway loss. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h8)

question: What physical sign indicates upper airway swelling and potential obstruction immediately following extubation?
explanation: Stridor is a high-pitched, musical breathing sound caused by narrowing of the upper airway from post-intubation laryngeal edema. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h9)

question: Why is suctioning performed right before removing an endotracheal tube during extubation?

options.A: To dry the vocal cords and prevent post-extubation hoarseness
options.B: To clear pooled secretions above the cuff so they do not enter the lungs
options.C: To measure the negative pressure capacity of the patient's lungs
options.D: To collapse the internal cuff so the tube slides out smoothly

explanation: Secretions accumulate above the cuff over time; removing them prevents aspiration into the lower respiratory tract as the tube comes out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h9)
